finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-1] Clerk webhook: non-idempotent user creation
File: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: The handler verifies Svix then calls await db.user.create({ data: { id, email, ... } }) on user.created with no existence check, no upsert, and no local dedupe; errors from duplicate keys are not caught.  
Impact: Retries or duplicate events will cause 500s and repeated failures (webhook retries), producing DB constraint errors and potential webhook backlog under signup spikes.  
Fix: Make the handler idempotent — use upsert or check existence before create, persist event IDs (unique) or swallow duplicate-key errors and return 200.

[AUTH-2] LiveKit webhook: no idempotency for join/leave increments
File: src/app/api/webhooks/livekit/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: participant_joined / participant_left handlers call db.room.update(... { currentUsers: { increment: 1 } }) / decrement without deduplicating events or recording event IDs.  
Impact: Duplicate or retried LiveKit events will inflate/deflate currentUsers, breaking room capacity enforcement and causing incorrect authorization/room admission decisions at scale.  
Fix: Add idempotency (persist event.id in a table with unique constraint) or reconcile counts transactionally (e.g., track per-participant presence) before increment/decrement.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-3] Hot per-request DB user lookups (no cache)
File: src/app/api/fetch_user/route.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: Handler calls await currentUser() then immediately runs db.user.findUnique({ where: { id: user.id } }) for each request, with no caching or session-store optimization.  
Impact: High frontend polling or many concurrent authenticated requests will translate directly to DB read QPS on the users table, causing DB overload at scale.  
Fix: Cache user profile lookups (e.g., Redis/memo layer, short-lived cache, or return Clerk session payload to clients) and avoid a DB round-trip on every request.

[AUTH-4] Clerk signups synced synchronously in webhook
File: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: New user provisioning is done inline in the webhook handler (await db.user.create) with no background queue or retry backoff.  
Impact: Burst signups will make the webhook handler synchronous-blocking and can cause delivery timeouts / worker saturation under high signup load.  
Fix: Push user creation to an async job/queue or perform an upsert with lightweight checks; ensure webhook responds quickly after queueing work.

--- INFO ---

[AUTH-5] Schema has provider/session unique indexes
File: prisma/schema.prisma
Evidence: Customer.clerk_user_id is @unique and stripe fields (stripe_customer_id, stripe_subscription_id) are unique or indexed, which makes provider lookups efficient.
